title: Detokenization Leaks: Reconstructing Local LLM Outputs From Cache Traces
abstract: arXiv:2609.06674v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present a new attack that reconstructs the text generated by locally hosted LLMs by observing CPU cache activity during detokenization. Unlike prior attacks that rely on deployment-specific assumptions, such as shared data memory, CPU offloading, or Mixture-of-Experts architectures, our approach targets the detokenizer, a component used in default LLM inference pipelines. To obtain clean signals, we use Flush+Reload on shared tokenizer code to detect when decoding occurs, which lets us perform Prime+Probe at the right moment and isolate token-dependent cache activity. We then apply a clustering-and-language-model pipeline to recover text from noisy cache observations. We evaluate the attack across multiple datasets, hardware platforms, inference frameworks, and model families, and show that it can recover semantically accurate outputs from real-world local LLM deployments, including agentic systems. translated_title: 去标记化泄露：从缓存痕迹重建本地LLM输出
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种新型攻击，通过观察去标记化过程中的CPU缓存活动来重建本地托管LLM生成的文本。与以往依赖特定部署假设（如共享数据内存、CPU卸载或混合专家架构）的攻击不同，我们的方法针对的是去标记器（detokenizer）——这是默认LLM推理管道中使用的一个组件。为了获得干净的信号，我们在共享的分词器代码上使用Flush+Reload技术检测解码发生的时机，这使我们能够在正确的时刻执行Prime+Probe并隔离与token相关的缓存活动。随后，我们应用聚类与语言模型相结合的流水线，从嘈杂的缓存观测数据中恢复文本。我们在多个数据集、硬件平台、推理框架和模型家族上评估了该攻击，结果表明它能够从真实世界的本地LLM部署（包括智能体系统）中恢复语义准确的输出。该漏洞对于……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种新型CPU缓存侧信道攻击，无需依赖特定部署假设，通过在去标记化过程中观测缓存活动并结合Flush+Reload、Prime+Probe技术及聚类与语言模型流水线，即可从本地部署的LLM中重建语义准确的生成文本。
